title: First experiment with RL
author: zjgkkn
selftext:
Hi, reddit!

A week ago, I shared an experiment with locally generated game assets. This time, I wanted to see if I could train a neural network to control enemies in combat.

The fighters learn entirely through self-play in Unity ML-Agents, using PPO. They fight copies of themselves and past versions of the network.

One of the biggest challenges was teaching them to move and react to their opponent. Adding a small LSTM memory made a noticeable difference: the fighters started adapting to their opponent's behaviour instead of repeating the same mistakes.

Training runs across 16 headless arenas on a laptop. 10 miiilons steps, \~10 hours.  
Videos above. Code and design doc: [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/blob/main/games/soulslike/training/README.md](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/blob/main/games/soulslike/training/README.md)

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body: I've come across YouTube videos about similar things before, and this seems like a great opportunity to learn more about actor-critic reinforcement learning. It's pretty fascinating and funny how agents find ways to exploit the reward mechanism in every way except the one intended ;)
